newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet sets terms for its Seat unit spin-off.
newsitem.headline: Stet sets terms for its Seat unit spin-off.

text.p: Italian state telecoms group Stet detailed conditions for the spin-off of its Seat yellow pages publishing division which it said was expected to take place by January 1997 when Seat will also be listed on the Milan bourse.
State industrial holding company IRI, which controls Stet, has already said it wants to spin-off Seat by the end of the year. Stet is slated for privatisation by March 1997.
Stet said in a statement the partial separation of Seat would create a new public company Seat SpA, with share capital of 264.1 billion lire and net assets of 560.4 billion lire.
Its capital will be divided into 5.28 billion shares of a nominal 50 lire each, comprising 3.83 billion ordinary and 1.45 billion savings shares.
Stet shareholders will receive Seat ordinary and savings shares on the basis of one new share for every Stet share held.

Stet said that to make up Seat's net assets it would use only reserves, leaving its share capital unchanged, and Stet's net assets at the end of the operation will therefore be reduced by 560.4 billion lire to 11.417 trillion lire.
The measures, approved by Stet's board on Friday, will be put to an extraordinary shareholders meeting for approval on October 28.

IRI on Thursday appointed Lehman Brothers advisor for the planned sale of Seat following its spin-off. Newspapers say the government hopes the sale will raise some three trillion lire, of which 1.4 trillion would go to IRI, which holds some 46.5 percent of Stet's total capital.
